verdicts.rationale: Clean reproduction confirmed: POST /collections/drop with collection_name='nonexistent_collection_xyz' succeeded with HTTP 200 and empty body, despite the collection never existing. Independent verification via has_collection() returns False, proving collection doesn't exist. Source code analysis (handler_v2.go:745-759) shows dropCollection handler performs NO existence check before proxy.DropCollection() call - it directly proceeds to deletion attempt. This allows dropping nonexistent collections to succeed silently, violating idempotency semantics and masking actual errors. This matches REST_v2_data_type_handling pattern - REST v2 fails to validate preconditions before state-changing operations.
